column3: The Hebrew says Solomon gave orders to build and calls both buildings houses, including a house for his kingship; BSB describes his purpose and a royal palace for himself.
The Hebrew explicitly names Solomon and says he counted the men; BSB uses he conscripted them.
The Hebrew begins as you did for my father without a separate do for me command; BSB supplies that command.
The Hebrew literally speaks of a continual arrangement without naming showbread and ends this is upon Israel forever; BSB explains the bread and an ordinance.
The Hebrew explicitly mentions possessing strength and making smoke before Him; BSB expresses ability and a place to burn sacrifices.
The Hebrew calls the craftsman and his coworkers wise and does not explicitly name yarn; engraving and engravings repeat one root.
The Hebrew repeats Lebanon as the location of cutting; BSB uses there.
The Hebrew calls the building the house; BSB specifies the temple.
The Hebrew uses a completed giving verb and does not specify olive oil; BSB says I will pay and specifies olive oil.
The Hebrew separately describes Hiram speaking in writing and sending it; BSB describes writing a letter in reply.
The Hebrew calls both buildings houses, including a house for his kingship; BSB specifies a temple and a royal palace for himself.
The Hebrew uses a completed sending verb and says the man knows understanding; BSB uses am sending and endowed with creativity.
The Hebrew speaks of designing a design rather than executing it and does not explicitly name yarn.
The Hebrew keeps my lord and his servants in the third person and says he spoke rather than promised.
The Hebrew explicitly says taking the timber up to Jerusalem; BSB uses can take.
The Hebrew ends with the supervisors causing the people to work; BSB leaves that purpose unstated.
